record.paper_title: On Structure and Open Problems in Topological Theories Coupled to Topological Gravity
record.context_brief: Defining topological gravity for massive topological theories
record.original_question: In a two-dimensional topological matter theory coupled to topological gravity, Q-exact terms in the action need not decouple because boundaries of the moduli space contribute anomalously. The paper states that this nondecoupling creates problems in defining topological gravity for massive topological theories, and later explains that the theory is well behaved for conformal regulators but that some theories may not admit such a regulator. Determine how topological gravity should be defined for massive topological theories in this setting, including what replaces a conformal regulator when no such regulator exists.

evidence.quote: This nondecoupling in the action of the theory is connected with the existence of boundaries of the moduli space and leads to problems in defining the topological gravity for massive topological theories.

Therefore, below we will consider only conformal regulators. If for some theories it is impossible to find such a regulator (this happens, for example, in topological sigma models of type A on manifolds with non-zero first Chern class) it seems that this theory should be considered in the asymptotically conformal limit, i.e., when the trace of G is very small and we can neglect it.

artifact.category_tag: topological gravity coupled to topological matter
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional topological matter theory with a nilpotent BRST-type operator Q, coupled to two-dimensional topological gravity. The coupling is realized by integrating correlation functions of the matter sector over the moduli space M_{g,n} of genus g Riemann surfaces with n marked points (or its Deligne–Mumford compactification). In the conformal case, Q-exact insertions in the action decouple from physical correlators. However, when the matter theory is massive (i.e. its stress tensor is not Q-exact, or more generally the theory is not conformally invariant), Q-exact terms in the action fail to decouple because integration by parts on the moduli space picks up anomalous boundary contributions from the compactification divisor.

A regulator of the matter theory is called conformal if it preserves Q-invariance and conformal invariance simultaneously, so that the boundary contributions vanish and topological gravity is well defined in the standard way. There exist topological matter theories for which no such conformal regulator exists; an example is the A-type topological sigma model whose target manifold has nonzero first Chern class.

Problem. Provide an intrinsic definition of two-dimensional topological gravity coupled to a massive topological matter theory in which Q-exact deformations of the action genuinely decouple from physical correlators, accounting for the anomalous boundary contributions from ∂M_{g,n}. In particular, when the matter theory does not admit a conformal regulator, specify a substitute (a modified regularization, a prescription for boundary contributions, or another construction) that replaces the role of a conformal regulator and yields a consistent, scheme-independent definition of the coupled topological gravity theory and its correlation functions.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a foundational definitional issue in topological gravity coupled to massive topological matter raised in the early 1990s. Subsequent literature on topological strings, gravitational descendants, and Gromov–Witten theory (Witten, Kontsevich, Dijkgraaf–Witten, and later cohomological field theory work) addresses related structures, but a direct, complete answer specifying how to define topological gravity for arbitrary massive topological matter theories without a conformal regulator does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature accessible here. Status is therefore recorded as unknown.
